title: Every excised specimen has a histology request
logic: If an operative record includes excision of any tissue (node, mass, ulcer edge, organ) and no histopathology request is attached, the operative record is incomplete — undiagnosed discarded tissue is an unrecoverable error.
action: Block operative-note finalisation until a histology request (with specimen orientation details where applicable) is linked, or an explicit senior-documented no-histology justification is recorded; open a results-tracking task automatically.

title: Fresh-specimen and TB routing arranged before node biopsy
logic: If an excisional lymph node biopsy is booked for suspected lymphoma, the laboratory pathway for a fresh (unfixed) specimen and for TB studies must be confirmed before induction — formalin destroys the immunophenotyping options and the node cannot be re-excised.
action: Add a specimen-routing confirmation checklist item to the booking; flag bookings without it; record in the operative note exactly which laboratory received which portion.

title: Sarcoma-pattern mass classifies to biopsy-first, never shell-out
logic: If a soft tissue mass is recorded as over 5 cm, deep to fascia, rapidly enlarging, or recurrent after previous excision, classify as suspected sarcoma: the pathway is imaging then core/incisional biopsy then MDT-planned wide excision at central hospital — direct excision (shell-out) is a pathway violation that contaminates the field and worsens survival.
action: Route sarcoma-pattern masses to the biopsy-first worklist; warn when an excision is being booked against an unbiopsied mass matching these criteria and require senior override with reason; auto-refer confirmed sarcoma histology to central MDT.

title: Changing chronic wound classifies to malignancy exclusion
logic: If a chronic wound, burn scar, or sinus is recorded with new changes — raised or everted edge, new nodularity, contact bleeding, or growth — classify to the Marjolin pathway: multi-quadrant edge biopsy before any further dressing-only plan.
action: Prompt edge biopsy ordering on matching wound-care records; flag wounds with documented change and no biopsy result within 4 weeks; route positive histology to EXPEDITED excision planning with reconstruction consult.

title: Oncological compression emergencies
logic: If a patient on any cancer pathway develops new limb weakness or sphincter disturbance (spinal cord compression), stridor or facial/arm swelling (airway or superior vena cava obstruction), these are oncological emergencies where hours change outcome.
action: Raise an emergency alert; immediate senior review and same-day referral to the appropriate emergency pathway (steroids per policy and urgent radiotherapy/oncology contact for cord compression); do not schedule as routine oncology review.

title: Early gastrostomy dislodgement is a surgical review
logic: If a surgically placed feeding gastrostomy tube is recorded as dislodged within about 4 weeks of placement (immature tract), blind ward-level reinsertion risks intraperitoneal placement and peritonitis.
action: Alert that reinsertion must be by the surgical team (with contrast confirmation where available); block the routine tube-change task type for tubes younger than the maturity threshold; advise nil-by-tube and review if placement is in doubt.

title: Proportionate prophylaxis for oncological surgery
logic: If an oncological procedure is booked, prophylaxis follows the wound class: single-dose cefazolin within 60 minutes before incision for clean cases with grafts, flaps, drains, or implants; add metronidazole where a gut lumen is opened (gastrostomy, colostomy); malnourished and immunosuppressed patients do not need prolonged prophylaxis — they need correctly timed single-dose prophylaxis plus nutritional attention.
action: Prompt wound-class-matched prophylaxis at induction with timing capture; flag postoperative continuation of prophylactic antibiotics beyond 24 hours as non-indicated.

title: Flap, graft and reconstruction surveillance
logic: If a flap or skin graft was used to close an oncological excision, viability observation (colour, capillary refill, congestion for flaps; bolster integrity for grafts) is due per protocol in the first 48–72 hours, because a failing flap salvaged early is a different outcome from one found at first dressing change.
action: Generate flap-observation tasks at the unit's protocol frequency for 72 hours; alert the surgical team on any recorded congestion, pallor, or bolster disruption; schedule first graft inspection at the protocol interval.

title: Histology results tracked to an actioned decision
logic: If an oncological specimen has been sent, the loop closes only when the result is reviewed, an MDT or senior decision is recorded, and the patient is informed — commonly within 4 weeks; margin-positive excisions specifically require a documented re-excision decision.
action: Keep the results-tracking task red until result-reviewed, decision-recorded, and patient-informed are all captured; escalate results older than 4 weeks without action to the responsible consultant; auto-flag margin-positive reports for a re-excision decision field.

title: Structured surveillance after curative oncological excision
logic: If a curative-intent excision is completed (sarcoma, melanoma, Marjolin SCC), a structured surveillance schedule per MDT is part of the treatment: commonly 3-monthly clinical review of the site and node basins in the first 2 years with chest imaging for sarcoma per protocol, then extending intervals; patients taught site and skin self-examination.
action: Auto-generate the MDT-specified surveillance schedule at histology sign-off; flag lapsed surveillance visits to the responsible clinic; attach self-examination education to the discharge record.
